about.title: About This Site
about.subtitle: You want to see China. The Chinese internet won't let you in. I go in and haul other people's eyes out for you.
about.brandStory: The name nods to Liu Cixin's short story 'With Her Eyes' (带上她的眼睛), by the author of The Three-Body Problem — a traveler carries a borrowed pair of eyes so that someone far away can see the world. We changed one word. To be clear: the eyes aren't mine. The Finnish family's eyes are theirs; the plank-walk POV belongs to the guy on Mount Hua. I'm just a middleman for eyes — I collect them from places you can't get into, inspect the goods, and put them on the shelf. The 'my' in the name is a street vendor's 'my': 'take my eyes' means 'take my wares'.
about.missionTitle: What Stands Between You and the World
about.offerSubtitle: No algorithm. Everything picked by a human.
about.ctaTitle: Borrow a Pair of Eyes First?
about.ctaSubtitle: See the real China through the screen — and when you finally make it here, the roads will still be there.
about.missionP1: Wanting to see a place has never been harder — not for lack of information, but because there's too much of it, too fake, too loud. Search engines hand you decade-old guidebooks and sponsored lists. Social feeds show you only what the algorithm wants you to see. AI can now generate ten thousand "first-hand guides" a day. And the walls don't stop at language and platforms — the algorithm is a wall too. Behind them: a flood of video no human could ever sift alone.
about.missionP2: Even if you climbed every wall, two more things would hold you back: money, and nerve. Flights aren't cheap. Visas feel like a lottery. There's the unfamiliar language, the rumors about payments, the quiet question — is it safe over there? Curiosity and fear grow up together. Just like the girl trapped at the center of the Earth: it's not that she didn't want to see. She couldn't get out. Wanting to see, through layers of rock — that's the ordinary human condition.
about.missionP3: So this site does one simple thing: it runs a middleman operation. I live on this side of the walls. I climb them for you, outbid the algorithms, and pull the few pairs of eyes actually worth your time out of the flood — the Finnish family's, the bus guy's, the dude on the plank walk — inspected, vetted, shelved. And when your wallet and your nerve are finally ready, go see it yourself. Until then: borrow a few eyes. See it from where you are.
